subject: how a 5-tick syndrome-measurement circuit sequences Z-checks, X-checks, an idle tick, and a final ancilla measurement

groups.why_chosen: AlphaSyndrome represents a syndrome-measurement schedule as a tick-divided circuit: each tick performs at most one Pauli check per qubit (Z-check via a plain CNOT, X-check via a Hadamard-CNOT-Hadamard sandwich) or leaves the ancilla explicitly idling, ending in a Z-basis measurement.
groups.what_to_learn: a standard quantum-circuit timeline with dashed vertical rules marking discrete scheduling ticks; a text callout with an arrow picking out one specific gate instance for discussion; reuse of a Hadamard-CNOT-Hadamard sandwich (established in an earlier figure) as a single compound 'X-check' unit
